learning: Check whether max_error still reaches 0.06 m on the s-bend (turn authority still limiting), whether progress rises on the oval and slalom with seven sensors, whether steering_oscillation rises with kp 4.0 and the wider track, and whether completion_time falls toward 3 s with the larger wheel at base_speed 1.4.
notes: Integrates the Builder's seven-sensor, larger-wheel, wider-track geometry with kp 4.0, kd 0.3, base_speed 1.4 and last_direction line loss. Raises turn authority because iteration 1 showed steady outward drift to the 0.06 m floor with low oscillation. The weights are scaled to the new lateral spread.
rationale: Iteration 1 evidence (60 trials, all off_track): progress 0.11 to 0.15, max_error at the 0.06 m floor on every track, rms_error about 0.025, line_loss about 1 per run, and steering_oscillation 0.10 to 0.14. The robot drifts outward steadily and is not jittering, so the controller is still too soft on bends. Iteration 1 changed gains and geometry together, so I cannot separate their effects, but raising kp from 3.2 to 4.0 is the most direct response to steady outward drift. The Builder's new geometry (7 sensors at y=0.07, 0.01 m spacing, wheel_radius 0.035, wheel_track 0.11) is kept unchanged so its intent is tested as written. The sensor weights are scaled to the new lateral positions as x/0.015, giving -2, -1.33, -0.67, 0, 0.67, 1.33, 2. This keeps the signal sign-correct (positive = left) and within the weight limit. kp rises to 4.0 for more turn authority, and kd rises from 0.2 to 0.3 to damp the faster response. ki stays at 0.15 to cancel the fixed motor mismatch. base_speed drops from 1.6 to 1.4, as the Builder expects, because off_track ends every run and a slower approach should keep the robot on the line. The larger wheel gives more speed at the same PWM, so 1.4 should still give a reasonable pace toward the 3 s limit. line_loss stays last_direction. Expected result: fewer off_track endings and higher progress on the s-bend. Completion is still unlikely and is not claimed.
